newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: Having raced up from the start of trade on Monday, South African industrial shares lost most of the ground they had earlier gained by afternoon and ended the day mildly above opening levels.
Heavy selling of stocks by active futures players dragged industrials off the highs they climbed out of relief that Wall Street did not lose as heavily as was expected.
"Stocks took a pounding from the futures guys who came in to sell shares and buy the futures. The indices slipped right back but still ended firmer," a dealer said.

While Wall Street did lose on Friday, after comments by Federal Reserve governor Alan Greenspan were interpreted to mean U.S. markets were overheated, the sheer relief that its fall was not more rejuvenated world stock markets.
Local industrials and all-shares powered up as renewed confidence in equitites triggered much buying at the low levels.
Dealers said heavyweight shares held their own amid much pressure from sellers and the majority ended well up.
"Heavyweights battled a bit under selling pressure but they kept their noses above water and finished firm," a dealer said.
Dealers said trade was fairly square and volumes moderate.
"There were pretty much as many declines as there were advances...about 31 million shares changed hands so volumes were moderate," another dealer said.
Earlier a firm bond market underpinned the equity market and dealers said that even after bonds softened slightly to become steady they supported equities.
Industrial shares rose 24.8 points to 7,820.0 and all-shares were pulled up 13.9 points at 6,615.1.
Gold shares were fairly motionless and traded just under opening levels all day, weighed by a dull bullion price. The gold index finished 9.7 points weaker at 1,517.8.
De Beers added 200 cents to 140 rand, Lonrho put on 32 cents to 932 cents and Amcoal shed 800 cents to 336 rand.
After starting the day strongly, industrial and all-share contracts also softened a tad by close, ending in the region of their previous settlememt levels.
The December all-share contract dipped a little to 5,960/6,000 from 5,990, the industrial contract was slightly firmer at 7,475/96 from 7,470 and the gold contract was at 1,045/75 from 1,068.
